claims.statement: The native MCP adapter exposes four reading tools by default and adds lifecycle tools only when constructed with a writer; successful results include JSON text and structured content.
Native wiki search uses an in-memory FTS5 index and ranks lexical matches by source-path boosts, term coverage, then weighted BM25 rather than filtering to hinted source paths.
Search retains at most four index sets and 32 MiB of page text, compares current page content on each search, and reuses unchanged page units when rebuilding after edits.
Section reads validate page paths and requested anchors, fail for missing anchors, and optionally return recorded provenance without rechecking claim freshness.

Workspace search is local for an unregistered repository, automatically selects a sole membership or active workspace, and otherwise returns workspace_required; linked reads require shared membership and valid materialized locations.
A writer accepts later lifecycle calls only for its active run ID, and begin resumes persisted state while discarding the old plan when source fingerprints have changed.
Plans reject duplicate and reserved pages, prohibit deleting quickstart, require quickstart for init, automatically add issue pages unless deferred, and sort quickstart last.

Page claim reconciliation retains omitted issue-free claims, requires explicit decisions for stale or unresolved claims, rejects duplicate decisions, and requires at least one claim per completed factual page.

Page completion follows persisted Markdown/frontmatter validation and claim reconciliation, with durability checks comparing the page hash, claim set, and verification projection before recording completion.
Evidence excludes Git metadata and generated wiki output, applies ignore rules before reads, rejects symlinks and aliases, and hashes whole files or relocatable line spans with context metadata.
Claim preflight records newly ignored or security-refused evidence as unresolved while propagating other resolver errors; changed resolved evidence is stale.
The authoring backend limits ordinary writes to wiki output and refuses claim paths and excluded paths, while claim sidecars use a dedicated contained store with atomic replacement.

Finish refuses pending jobs, reconciles deletions and orphaned sidecars, finalizes indexes, links, source and provenance fields, and leaves freshness interrupted for deferred claims or detected source drift.

Concurrent searches sharing a retained wiki-root scope serialize index building and ranking through one mutex-protected SQLite index slot, so matching cold searches build once and waiting searches reuse that index.
Incremental retrieval rebuilds reuse unchanged parsed page units and can parse changed pages with up to eight workers, further limited by available parallelism and changed-text size.
A failed search-index rebuild returns its error without replacing the previous cached index or serving that previous index as a fallback result for changed content.

The retrieval Markdown lexer grows its stack as needed and returns TooDeep when parsing exceeds its 3,000-level nesting limit, 16 MiB cumulative work budget, or 1,048,576 emphasis/strikethrough closing-delimiter scans; work includes nested text and remaining inline text at each rule-attempt position, so costly headings can fail without exceeding nesting depth.
A retrieval parser-limit failure fails the affected search or section-read call with the generic OpenWiki MCP operation error while leaving a subsequent read of another valid page usable.
Desktop wiki page presentation uses core's MarkdownRenderer rather than retrieval's lexer, and has its own small-stack deep-page regression coverage.
Begin checks canonical repository containment for the wiki folder and setup destinations, refusing outward file, parent, and dangling symlinks while supporting links resolving inside the repository.

The model-free update preflight checks whether existing pages have complete coverage, were edited after verification, or cite changed resources, and whether files were added or source definitions/large changes suggest material new facts; it records an update only when these checks and source-stability checks pass.

For likely-new-fact detection, added files are considered separately from changed source files; changed source paths are flagged for new definitions or keys, or at least 50 changed lines, while small declaration-only changes under recognized test paths are excluded.

The changed-source detector treats Git listing or diff failures as uncertainty rather than proof of no relevant changes, so the preflight requires a model-backed update instead of silently recording a no-op.

The quiet update preflight starts a writing run for unresolved/stale claims, hand-edited or uncovered pages, added files, and changed source files with detected new declarations or at least 50 changed lines; it records a no-model update only when the evidence and coverage checks pass and source remains stable through finalization.

The preflight's source-change heuristic detects declarations and newly introduced keys across supported source files, ignores declaration-only changes in test paths, and treats large diffs as update-worthy; the detector uses controlled Git diff options and separately checks file names to avoid silently missing unparsed paths.
